builds.name: Reference: Critical carry
builds.goal: Reference for Kindred: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: A mobile ranged hunter who uses a defined Wolf zone for repeated short dashes and attacks. Marks increase future reach and ability effectiveness, while R requires careful end-of-zone timing. Fix mark count, W zone and E execute setup. R can protect the opponent too; judge damage and health at zone expiry rather than an immortal target dummy. Attack cadence, crit and penetration support repeatable carry damage.
builds.summary: Attack cadence, crit and penetration support repeatable carry damage.
testPlan: Kit question for Kindred: Fix mark count, W zone and E execute setup. R can protect the opponent too; judge damage and health at zone expiry rather than an immortal target dummy.

Start with the early core (Kraken, then Infinity Edge) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Attack cadence, crit and penetration support repeatable carry damage. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Kindred tumbles and shoots up to three arrows at nearby targets. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Crit is valuable only for effects that can crit; low defense makes positioning decisive.
The route fails Kindred's stated kit question: Fix mark count, W zone and E execute setup. R can protect the opponent too; judge damage and health at zone expiry rather than an immortal target dummy.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Crit is valuable only for effects that can crit; low defense makes positioning decisive.
Full cost 16,950 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
The reference is a research control, not a claim of the current highest-win-rate build.
buyOrder: Kraken, then Infinity Edge. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Phantom Dancer, Lord Dominik's Regards, Bloodthirster are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

Kindred vaults, firing an arrow at up to 3 enemies, dealing [40 / 65 / 90 / 115 / 140 + (0.75) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage and gaining [0.35 + (0.05) × BuffStacks({64290302})] Attack Speed for [4] seconds.

While inside of {{Spell_KindredW_Name}}, this Ability's Cooldown is reduced to [4 / 3.5 / 3 / 2.5 / 2] seconds.

Passive: Kindred gains stacks as they move and attack. At 100 stacks, Kindred's next Attack restores up to [characterLevelBreakpoints(start=47, perLevel=2, changes=[])] Health based on their missing Health.

Active: Kindred claims a territory, ordering Wolf to bite at the last enemy Lamb Attacked. Wolf's bites deal [25 / 30 / 35 / 40 / 45 + (0.2) × AD[statFormula=2] + (0.2) × AP] plus [0.015 + (0.01) × BuffStacks({64290302})] current Health magic damage.

Kindred can designate a champion to hunt by clicking their portrait above their inventory. They also designate certain jungle monsters to hunt with an icon on the minimap automatically.

Getting a takedown on a hunted target grants Kindred a Mark, empowering them. After [4] Marks, Kindred gains [(25) × (3)] Attack Range. Every [3] Marks after the fourth grants a further [25] Attack Range.

Marks empower Kindred's basic Abilities:{{Spell_KindredQ_Name}} grants an additional [(0.05) × BuffStacks({64290302})] Attack Speed{{Spell_KindredW_Name}} deal an additional [(0.01) × BuffStacks({64290302})] current Health damage.{{Spell_KindredEWrapper_Name}} deal an additional [(0.005) × BuffStacks({64290302})] missing Health damage.

Kindred blesses the ground for [4] seconds, allowing no unit, ally, enemy, or neutral to die while inside. Upon reaching 10% Health, units can't be damaged or healed while still inside the zone.

When the blessing ends, all units inside heal for [225 / 300 / 375] Health.

Kindred weakens an enemy, Slowing them by [30 + (0.05) × AP]% for [1.5] second.

Kindred's third Attack against the target within [4] seconds of each other directs Wolf to pounce on the enemy, dealing an additional [(80 / 110 / 140 / 170 / 200 + (1) × AD[statFormula=2]) × ((1 + ((0.5) × Stat(8)) × (((1) × Stat(9) + -1))))] plus [(0.05 + (0.005) × BuffStacks({64290302})) × ((1 + ((0.5) × Stat(8)) × (((1) × Stat(9) + -1))))] missing Health physical damage.

builds.name: Wolf AP territory
builds.summary: Test wolf ap territory against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test wolf ap territory against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Wolf's Frenzy bites include 0.2 AP magic damage and marks add current-health damage; Nashor supports Lamb's actual attacks while Gunblade retains AD for Q/E. Bloodletter fits W magic pressure only if wolf attribution is confirmed; territory makes frequent Q repositioning possible.
testPlan: Required state: Use a recorded realistic mark count and keep enemies inside W.
Compare Wolf-only damage and Lamb attacks across one territory.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Wolf uptime and low AD may lose the E execute despite stronger W.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Wolf cannot be assumed to inherit Nashor on-hits or owner attack speed.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Nashor's Tooth, Hextech Gunblade, Bloodletter's Curse, Riftmaker, Banshee's Veil, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Respite spell duelist

builds.goal: Test respite spell duelist against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Inside Wolf's Frenzy, Dance of Arrows cooldown falls to two seconds at max rank; Essence Reaver gives physical Spellblade between Qs. Hexplate supports attacks after Lamb's Respite, while crit improves E's documented source expression; Shojin rewards repeated physical ability use.
testPlan: Required state: Time Q and E so damage lands after Respite's four-second protection.
Record Q attacks, E finish and health after both sides exit R.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.

The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.

Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
